properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 20 at 1:42AM EDT until September 20 at 7:45AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Meigs County in southeastern Ohio...
Southwestern Washington County in southeastern Ohio...
North Central Jackson County in northwestern West Virginia...
Wood County in northwestern West Virginia...
North Central Mason County in western West Virginia...

* Until 745 AM EDT Sunday.

* At 142 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Parkersburg, Athens, Marietta, Belpre, Pomeroy, Coolville, Rutland,
Forked Run State Park, Vienna, Williamstown, New Haven, Mason,
Tuppers Plains, Washington, Lubeck, Mineralwells, Boaz, Middleport,
Chester and North Hills.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 77 in West Virginia near mile marker 151...and between
mile markers 164 and 186. Route 50 in West Virginia between mile
markers 1 and 13.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 20 at 1:38AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
At 138 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from near Belmont to near Ravenswood to near
Rutland. Movement was southeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Parkersburg, Marietta, Belpre, Ripley, Harrisville, Pomeroy,
Elizabeth, Racine, Rutland, Forked Run State Park, Vienna,
Ravenswood, New Haven, Pennsboro, Mason, Belmont, Sandyville,
Mineralwells, Washington, and North Bend State Park.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 77 in West Virginia between mile markers 139 and 185.
Route 50 in West Virginia between mile markers 1 and 45.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to travel across
flooded roads. Find alternate routes. It takes only a few inches of
swiftly flowing water to carry vehicles away.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 20 at 1:32AM AST until September 20 at 3:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...All of Puerto Rico, including Vieques and Culebra, and the
U.S. Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 20 at 2:22PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Yap State with a few areas of stronger
gusts north of Faraulep.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. By
midweek, models indicate the potential for a circulation to slowly
organize as it passes between Yap and Guam into the Philippine Sea.
As this happens, westerly winds and gusts will increase with showers
and thunderstorms. While these conditions will generally be felt
across Yap State, portions of the Republic of Palau could see heavy
showers and thunderstorms dropping south early in the week.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 19 at 1:47PM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A series of low pressure systems will move through the panhandle
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway and Haines.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Current thinking is
that the light rain will continue Saturday evening before a
second, stronger system moves in for Saturday night into Sunday
morning bringing moderate to heavy rain fall. Rain showers will
then take over on Sunday that may bring occasional moderate to
heavy rainfall as well.

For the Skagway area, 24 hour precip looks to get up to 1 to 2
inches this weekend while the storm total amounts could be 2 to 4
inches. The Haines area is expected to see 0.75 to 1.5 inches in
24 hours while a storm total precipitation of 2 to 3.5 inches is
possible.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 19 at 11:59AM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
ESFRIW

Periods of showers and thunderstorms are expected across the northern
half of Wyoming Saturday and Sunday as a wet weather system shifts
east across the state. This weather system is funneling abundant
tropical moisture into northern and eastern portions of the state
with it's eastward progression. Given the high moisture content, many
thunderstorms could feature heavy rainfall and possibly lead to
localized flooding. Poor drainage areas, urban areas, and steep
terrain will be the most susceptible locations for this isolated
flooding.

Many locations could see an additional 0.5" to 1.25" of rain through
Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling quickly in
thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

NWSheadline: Showers and Thunderstorms Could Produce Heavy Rainfall and Localized Flooding through Sunday

properties.areaDesc: Yellowstone National Park; Absaroka Mountains; Cody Foothills; Owl Creek and Bridger Mountains; Bighorn Mountains West; Bighorn Mountains Southeast; Northeast Johnson County; Southeast Johnson County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 19 at 11:54AM MDT until September 20 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by moderate to heavy rainfall is
possible, especially in terrain and poor drainage areas.

* WHERE...Portions of central, north central, and northwest Wyoming,
including the following areas, in central Wyoming, Owl Creek and
Bridger Mountains. In north central Wyoming, Bighorn Mountains
Southeast, Bighorn Mountains West, Northeast Johnson County and
Southeast Johnson County. In northwest Wyoming, Absaroka Mountains,
Cody Foothills and Yellowstone National Park.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas and around
steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A slow moving weather system will move across Wyoming today and
Sunday and bring rounds of showers and thunderstorms to the
region, especially northern Wyoming. Any shower or thunderstorm
could produce moderate to heavy rainfall across the Watch Area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 19 at 10:19AM CDT until September 20 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Peak Heat Index values up to around 100 degrees this
weekend.

* WHERE...All of southern Illinois, southwest Indiana, western
Kentucky, and southeast Missouri.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT /8 PM EDT/ Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Heat Advisory was extended thru the
weekend due to the prolonged high heat conditions that have
basically been ongoing for the entirety of the past week; this
continues to heighten the risk of heat-related health impacts.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Allegan; Barry; Van Buren; Kalamazoo; Calhoun
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 19 at 11:17AM EDT until September 20 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Grand Rapids MI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Michigan, including
the following counties, in south central Michigan, Calhoun. In
southwest Michigan, Allegan, Barry, Kalamazoo and Van Buren.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain has fallen across the Flood Watch area.
Some localized ponding of water has been reported. This afternoon
will bring a lull in the activity, however more rain will spread
in this evening and continue through the night. Precipitation is
expected to taper off Sunday morning. The rain that has fallen
already has saturated the ground and additional rainfall will go
into run off and potential flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Chena River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 19 at 4:22AM AKDT until September 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River and stream flows
remain elevated. Ponding of water in areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 412 AM AKDT, gage reports indicated widespread moderate to
heavy rain across the Chena River Basin over the past several
days. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain has fallen this week.

- High water levels will continue to work through the Fairbanks,
Badger, and North Pole region along the Chena and Little Chena
Rivers. Use extra caution on and along the rivers as water levels
continue to run at near record to record levels for this time of
year. The Chena River near Two Rivers is dropping but remains
bankfull. The Chena River below Hunts Creek is dropping but
remains bankfull. The Chena River below Moose Creek Dam is
cresting. The Chena River at Fairbanks will be cresting Saturday
afternoon. We are expecting rivers to remain high through the
weekend but gradually drop towards more normal levels through the
week.

- For Chena River below Hunts Creek near Two Rivers :
At 4:00am the stage was 15.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 17.2 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 15.3 feet is expected at 10:00am
Saturday.


For Chena River below Moose Creek dam:
At 4:00am the stage was 24.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 24.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 24.8 feet is expected at 10:00am
Saturday.


For Chena River near Two Rivers:
At 3:00am the stage was 19.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 19.1 feet is expected at 10:00am
Saturday.


- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown, when encountering flooded roads.
